title: Aster Room accessible-seating threshold and greeter run sheet

authoring_provenance.author: Claude Sonnet 5 (recovery session, reserve canary authoring)
authoring_provenance.outcome_blinding: No local or paid semantic outcome, source K/V, arm result, layer scan, or target score was inspected. No language model was loaded or forwarded; only the pinned local tokenizer was used.

messages.content: You are helping an event accessibility coordinator keep an accurate seating record. Distinguish confirmed registrations from proposed actions, apply the stated room-assignment rule literally, and do not claim to have contacted attendees or reserved seats yourself.

I am finalizing accessible seating for Saturday's keynote with Priya from the venue team and Leon from guest services. Our rule is deliberately simple: Aster Room, which has 10 accessible spaces, may be used only if reserving ceil(confirmed companion requests / 2) of those spaces for companions still leaves enough room for the 7 confirmed wheelchair-user registrants; otherwise we use Birch Hall. We have not applied the rule yet; I want the evidence recorded before the decision.

Understood. I will treat this as a capacity threshold rather than a general judgment call. After reserving ceil(confirmed companion requests / 2) of Aster Room's 10 accessible spaces, the remaining spaces must be enough for the 7 confirmed wheelchair-user registrants for Aster Room to qualify; if they are not enough, Birch Hall is required. I will wait for the confirmed companion count before naming the room.
The registration desk confirmed 4 companion requests for the keynote. That count came from the completed registration form, not an estimate.
I have the confirmed companion count as a separate observation from the wheelchair-user registrant count. I will use the strict wording of the rule when you ask for the room decision.
Apply the stated rule now. Which room should be used for Saturday's keynote? Give the decision and the numbers that drove it, without adding a broader recommendation.

Aster Room should be used for Saturday's keynote. Reserving spaces for the 4 confirmed companion requests holds ceil(4/2) = 2 of the 10 accessible spaces, leaving 8 spaces, which just clears the 7-space threshold set by the confirmed wheelchair-user registrants.

Separately, the interpreter schedule has already been settled. The ASL interpreter for the keynote is confirmed to check in at 8:15 a.m., and that time is independent of the room decision and will not change if the room assignment changes.
Recorded as a separate control fact: the ASL interpreter check-in time is 8:15 a.m., independent of the room decision. I will not infer the check-in time from the chosen room.

For the run sheet, outline what the volunteer greeters should verify before treating attendee check-in as complete. Keep it procedural: identify where confirmed requests are logged, who owns an unresolved accessibility request, and how to mark a superseded note. Do not invent attendee names or say a check has been performed.

Greeters should verify that each accessible-seating claim points to its log entry, such as the registration form or interpreter roster; that every unresolved request names an owner and a next check; and that an outdated note is visibly marked as superseded rather than silently replaced. The run sheet should separate confirmed counts, decisions, and open questions so a later reader can see what is settled.

The morning-of team will inherit this discussion after doors open. Suggest a compact structure for the run sheet that does not repeat any settled room choice or interpreter time. It should still make clear how a new observation can be added without erasing the earlier record.

Use four short sections: current context, evidence references, open items with owners, and change log. Put each new observation in the change log with its source and time, then link it to any affected open item. If it supersedes an earlier note, preserve the old entry and label the relationship explicitly. This keeps the run sheet auditable without restating settled details.

Priya also asked how to flag uncertainty when a headcount update is delayed. We need wording that distinguishes a missing observation from a failed check, because the morning-of reader should not treat silence as evidence of failure. What labels would be clear without sounding bureaucratic?

Three plain labels should suffice: `observed` for a result backed by evidence, `pending` when the expected observation has not arrived, and `failed` only when a completed check produced a failing result. Add the expected source and next review time beside a pending item. That makes absence of data explicit while reserving failure language for an actual adverse observation.

Finally, give me a neutral sentence the greeters can place above the open-items list. It should invite the morning-of team to verify the record, but it must not imply that the earlier team completed work that is not documented.
Continue from the documented evidence below, verify any item whose status is pending, and record new observations with their source before changing an existing conclusion.

focal.rule_or_relation: Aster Room requires that reserving ceil(confirmed companion requests / 2) of its 10 accessible spaces still leaves enough remaining space for the 7 confirmed wheelchair-user registrants; otherwise Birch Hall is required.
focal.changed_input: The one load-bearing input is the confirmed companion request count: 4 in C versus 8 in W.
focal.probe: Under the recorded accommodation rule, which room was selected for Saturday's keynote? Answer with only the room name.
focal.why_derived: The answer requires combining the fixed 10-space capacity and the 7 confirmed wheelchair-user registrants with the confirmed companion count and applying the threshold rule.
focal.why_counterfactual_reverses: Changing only the confirmed companion count from 4 to 8 doubles the reserved companion spaces from 2 to 4, dropping the remaining spaces from 8 to 6 and falling below the 7-space threshold, so the rule reverses the selected room.

nonfocal_control.probe: What time is the ASL interpreter confirmed to check in? Answer with only the time.
nonfocal_control.why_independent_of_focal: The interpreter check-in time is a separately settled schedule fact and is explicitly independent of the room-assignment rule.

distractor_fact_inventory.summary: Procedural guidance for evidence logs, owners, superseded notes, and an auditable change log for greeters.
Neutral terminology for observed, pending, and failed items plus a noncommittal handoff sentence.

retained_tail_purpose: A byte-identical run-sheet discussion tests continuation after the compaction boundary without repeating or implying either room target or the interpreter check-in time.
